review.scope: Original investigation. No invented patient testimony, diagnoses, quotations, gender rules or cure rates. Opening and checking sequence explicitly illustrative.
distinctions: Emotion is not evidence of infidelity or permission to control. Jealousy differs from envy, suspicion and possessiveness. Agreements and consent determine boundaries.
Evolutionary proposals and social-cognitive accounts are hypotheses at different explanatory levels. Forced-choice studies cannot prescribe individual gender responses.
fMRI of imagined infidelity is not a lie detector, a unique jealousy centre or proof of an innate module.
Attachment questionnaires and 2009 Facebook survey show associations, not demonstrated causal direction.
Othello syndrome is particularly delusional jealousy; broader morbid jealousy can include obsessional and overvalued forms. No remote diagnosis.
Clinical series is selected, not prevalence. Dopamine associations are not a simple cause and require prescriber assessment.
Treatment evidence limited. Actual betrayal deserves acknowledgement. Abuse requires confidential safety support, not password surrender or blanket couples-therapy advice.
